newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court issues arrest warrant against Rao.
newsitem.headline: Indian court issues arrest warrant against Rao.

text.p: An Indian judge issued a warrant on Friday for the arrest of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in a forgery case, compounding the political leader's legal woes.

The Press Trust of India said that Rao's counsel immediately asked another court to provide the former prime minister with legal protection from arrest in the seven-year-old case, one of several involving the former Congress party leader.
The warrant empowered authorities to arrest Rao, but legal experts said he was not expected to be detained as the judge set a hearing date of October 14 to take up the charges.
The judge issued similar warrants against three others, including two who had not yet been charged in the case.
Two others who had been charged were in judicial custody. The judge issued warrants for them to appear in court on October 14.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's federal police, charged Rao and three others on September 26 in the forgery case involving an alleged attempt in 1989 to tarnish the reputation of V.P. Singh, an opposition leader who later became prime minister.
The case involves the alleged falsification of bank documents to show that Singh's son, Ajeya Singh, had a secret bank account with large amounts of money on the Caribbean island of St Kitts.
At the time V.P. Singh, who had left the ruling Congress party for the opposition, was spearheading an anti-corruption campaign against the government.

V.P. Singh was appointed prime minister at the end of 1989 after Congress lost a general election. Authorities later cleared Ajeya Singh of allegations that he had violated foreign exchange and anti-corruption laws.

A CBI statement last week said its investigation "revealed that the accused persons, in conspiring with each other, fabricated false evidence with the intent and knowledge to...harm their (V.P. Singh and Ajeya Singh) reputation in the eyes of the public".

The federal police agency said the four accused were charged with criminal conspiracy, forgery, giving false evidence and using forged documents. It did not say what possible penalties the charges carried.
Rao was not believed to have commented publicly on the case.
Rao stepped down as leader of the Congress party on September 21 after a Delhi judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court to face criminal conspiracy charges in a separate cheating case.

His court appearance in that case, scheduled for last Monday, was postponed until October 9 after the Supreme Court said it would take up a police request for the venue of the hearing to be shifted from a local court to a more secure spot.
